papers.title_en: Adapting Monocular Depth Estimation in Novel Scenes through Disparity Refinement and Robot Ego-Motion
papers.authors: Dimitrios Chatziparaschis, Georgios Georgakis, Adnan I. Ansar, Shehryar Khattak, Konstantinos Karydis
papers.evidence: 将单目深度基础模型的相对深度在新场景中自适应到度量尺度
papers.tldr: 单目深度基础模型多依赖仿射不变深度表示，迁移到新场景时度量尺度缺失、泛化性不明，而 LiDAR 和双目相机成本高。作者提出 EM-ViT，把基础模型输出的相对深度作为先验，借鉴双目相机参数化方式，将预测分解为稠密视差细化与有效基线标量估计，在线学习恢复场景结构与缺失的度量尺度。方法利用稀疏 LiDAR 点和机器人自运动，快速训练轻量 ViT，并用内部梯度匹配损失实时保持输入的细粒度语义结构。在 KITTI 等公开序列上，该在线学习流程比现有 MDE 基础模型适应新场景更快、精度更高，为机器人低成本稠密长距感知提供了可行方案。
papers.abstract_en: The geometric understanding of a scene is a crucial component for safe and efficient robotic operations in novel and unstructured environments. The recent emergence of foundation models for Monocular Depth Estimation (MDE) has provided an opportunity to enrich robotic perception capabilities with dense long-range depth predictions, replacing expensive onboard hardware (e.g., LiDARs and stereo cameras). However, these offline models are primarily trained on affine-invariant depth representations, and their generalization to novel scenes remains unclear. In this work we present EM-ViT, a monocular depth estimation model that learns to adapt online relative depth inputs from a foundation model prior to the metric scale with observations collected during robotic operations. Motivated by the stereo camera parameterization, our method decomposes depth prediction via dense disparity refinement to recover the scene's relative structure and an effective baseline scalar prediction to determine the missing metric scale. The learning process leverages sparse LiDAR points and, optionally, the robot's Ego-Motion (EM) to rapidly train a lightweight Vision Transformer (ViT), while an internal gradient matching loss preserves the fine-grained semantic structure of the input disparity in real-time. We demonstrate the efficacy of our method on publicly available sequences, such as KITTI, and show that our online learning pipeline can adapt to novel scenes faster and with higher accuracy than existing MDE foundation models. The code and supplementary materials will be publicly available at https://emvit-mde.github.io.

papers.title_en: EG360: Efficient and Generalizable $360^\circ$ Depth Estimation via Adaptive Panorama-Perspective Distillation and Spherical Cross-Level Feature Fusion
papers.authors: Laiyan Ding, Chongxi Meng, Rui Huang
papers.evidence: 轻量级深度模型的零样本全景深度估计
papers.tldr: 全景深度估计的泛化方法依赖大模型、算力开销高，难以在嵌入式平台实时运行；而轻量全景模型又多局限于单域评估、跨域泛化差。EG360在轻量深度模型基础上，提出由场景几何引导的自适应全景-透视蒸馏APPD，并设计球面跨层级特征融合SCFF模块增强全局语义感知。重参数化后仅6.593M参数，在真实基准上取得强零样本性能，Jetson Orin NX 16GB MAXN模式下达35 FPS。该工作弥合了高精度泛化模型与轻量模型之间的鸿沟，为嵌入式全景深度估计提供了高效可泛化方案。
papers.abstract_en: Generalized panorama depth estimation has witnessed great advances in recent years. These methods typically achieve robust zero-shot generalization performance using large pretrained models, but their high computational cost makes real-time inference on embedded platforms challenging. In contrast, previous lightweight panorama models have mostly been developed for single-domain evaluations and cannot generalize well due to domain shifts. To reduce the gap between these two types of models, we introduce EG360, an efficient and generalizable panorama depth estimation model. Specifically, building on a lightweight depth model, we design an Adaptive Panorama-Perspective Distillation (APPD) strategy guided by scene geometry, along with a Spherical Cross-Level Feature Fusion (SCFF) module for global semantic perception. As a result, with only 6.593M parameters after reparameterization, EG360 achieves strong zero-shot performance on real-world benchmarks and runs at 35 FPS on a Jetson Orin NX 16GB in MAXN mode, whereas a previous ViT-small model runs at less than 2 FPS. Our code will also be made public for future research.

papers.title_en: Iris-Z: Scaling One Generative Model Past Specialist Geometry Models
papers.evidence: 面向单目几何的统一生成模型
papers.tldr: 单目几何长期依赖专用架构，而语言领域已证明统一生成模型可随数据、参数和算力持续提升。Iris-Z 将外观与几何统一到单一生成骨干中，同一套权重可联合生成图像与深度、从照片估计深度，并依据给定深度生成图像。在足够规模下，它在既有深度基准上超过专用最先进模型，同时保留原生成能力且无需专门层。该工作验证了视觉与3D任务也应走统一架构和规模化路线，并公开两个模型。
papers.abstract_en: Language moved from many task-specific models to one unified model: a single generative model with a single generative training task that handles all of them within the same backbone, and keeps improving with data, parameters and compute. We believe the bitter lesson applies just as much to computer vision, 3D and spatial understanding, in the end to visual intelligence: the effort should go into general architectures that solve all these tasks in a unified way, and into scaling them, rather than into task-specific designs. We test this on monocular geometry, a task that has belonged to specialised architectures for years. Iris-Z is a general image generator that produces appearance and geometry together. A single backbone denoises, reasons about and understands the image and its depth at the same time, and one set of weights generates images with their depth, estimates depth from photographs and paints images onto a given depth. At enough scale it surpasses state-of-the-art specialists on established depth benchmarks while keeping the generative abilities of the backbone it started from without specialized layers. We release two models for the community.

papers.title_en: Kosmo-GFM: A Production-Ready Geometry Foundation Model
papers.authors: Sheng Tang, Shengzhe Wei, Tiancheng Chen, Wenhua Jin, Xinyang Lu, Tinghao Jiang, Shuoxuan Feng, Yupeng Liu, Yu Zhang, Xingshuo Chang, Keren Zhou, Yuhan Xiong, Jiahao Li, Haoming Liu, Jituo Tian, Hui Liang, Chaoqun Tang, Feng Tian, Wentao Ouyang, Kaojin Zhu, Xiaolin Chai, Peihuang Fu, Miao Zheng, Yunbo Hu, Feixue Cai, Zizhen Zou, Weigang Wang, Yexuan Yang, Haoyu Feng, Weiqi Zhang, Juntong Fang, Zesong Li
papers.evidence: 预测深度与度量几何的几何基础模型
papers.tldr: 场景重建需要可靠几何先验与相机位姿。Kosmo-GFM将几何基础模型GFM、位姿优化引擎PoseEngine和KosmoWorld结合：GFM预测相机参数、深度、跨视图对应与动态3D点，PoseEngine用几何优化恢复场景位姿和几何，KosmoWorld由重建场景生成监督以改进GFM。SpatialBench稀疏/中等子集上深度误差最低、5度相对位姿AUC最高，动态点与场景流端点误差最低；34场景位姿AUC最高，耗时14.07小时约GLUEMAP的20%，Flash版2.62小时约4%。这支持在场景级重建中采用学习几何先验。
papers.abstract_en: We present Kosmo-GFM, a scene reconstruction system that integrates a geometry foundation model (GFM), a pose optimization engine (PoseEngine), and reconstruction-derived supervision from KosmoWorld. GFM predicts camera parameters, depth, cross-view correspondences, and dynamic 3D points from images and videos. PoseEngine combines these predictions with geometric optimization to recover scene-level camera poses and geometry for downstream 3D and 4D Gaussian Splatting. KosmoWorld generates images and geometric supervision from reconstructed real-world scenes to improve GFM's geometric predictions. On the Sparse and Medium subsets of SpatialBench, GFM achieves the lowest absolute relative depth error and the highest relative-pose AUC at 5 degrees among the compared methods. It also achieves the lowest mean endpoint errors for dynamic points and scene flow across the five evaluated datasets. Across 34 scenes completed by all compared reconstruction systems, PoseEngine achieves the highest scene-averaged pose AUC at thresholds of 1, 3, and 5 degrees, with a cumulative runtime of 14.07 hours, approximately 20% of GLUEMAP's 69.67 hours. PoseEngine Flash provides a further accuracy-efficiency trade-off, with a measured mixed-precision runtime of 2.62 hours, approximately 4% of GLUEMAP's runtime. Separate scaling experiments show generally favorable trends with increased data, model computation, and training budgets. These results support the use of learned geometric priors within a scene-level reconstruction pipeline.
